headline: OpenAI Slashes GPT-5.6 Luna Prices by 80% Amid AI Price War
summary: The AI giant is aggressively cutting costs for its frontier models, making Luna significantly cheaper than Google's Gemini Flash models.
details: OpenAI has announced substantial price reductions for its GPT-5.6 frontier series models, with GPT-5.6 Luna seeing an 80% price cut and GPT-5.6 Terra reduced by 20%. This move intensifies the ongoing AI price wars, directly challenging competitors like Google and Anthropic.

GPT-5.6 Luna, now priced at $0.20 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens, becomes significantly more competitive, costing less than Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite. This positions OpenAI's smallest and fastest model for high-throughput, low-latency tasks.

The mid-tier GPT-5.6 Terra also receives a 20% price cut, bringing its combined cost to $14 per million tokens, matching Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview pricing. This adjustment aims to balance capability and efficiency for general production use.

OpenAI is also introducing a 'Fast mode' for its flagship GPT-5.6 Sol model, offering up to 2.5 times the throughput at double the standard price. This premium option targets latency-sensitive workloads, reflecting a strategic pricing approach for different use cases.

These aggressive pricing changes follow closely behind Anthropic's release of Claude Opus 5 and Google's introduction of new Gemini Flash models, indicating a market-wide shift towards more cost-effective AI solutions. OpenAI aims to sway users by offering both lower costs and enhanced speed.
